title: Within-Family EfficientNet Scaling under Fixed-Resolution Transfer Learning for Spectral-Domain Optical Coherence Tomography Retinal Disease Classification
abstract: arXiv:2611.06452v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Background/Objectives: CNNs perform well in retinal disease classification from spectral-domain optical coherence tomography (SD-OCT), but whether EfficientNet's natural-image scaling hierarchy transfers to medical-image transfer learning at fixed resolution remains unclear. This study evaluates EfficientNet-B0-B7 for four-class SD-OCT classification and accuracy-efficiency trade-offs. Methods: Eight ImageNet-pretrained variants (4.05-64.10M instantiated backbone parameters) were evaluated at 224x224 on the Kermany dataset. Grayscale images were replicated to RGB and processed using model-embedded preprocessing and augmentation. Training comprised frozen-backbone head training followed by partial fine-tuning. Metrics covered classification, discrimination, efficiency, and visual analyses. Results: Test accuracy varied non-monotonically from 95.93% (B0) to 96.95% (B1); B7 achieved 96.73%. translated_title: 固定分辨率迁移学习下的EfficientNet家族内缩放用于频域光学相干断层扫描视网膜疾病分类
translated_abstract: 背景/目的：卷积神经网络（CNN）在基于频域光学相干断层扫描（SD-OCT）的视网膜疾病分类中表现良好，但EfficientNet在自然图像上的缩放层级能否迁移到固定分辨率的医学图像迁移学习中仍不明确。本研究评估了EfficientNet-B0至B7在SD-OCT四分类任务中的表现以及准确率与效率之间的权衡。方法：在Kermany数据集上以224×224分辨率评估了八个ImageNet预训练变体（实例化骨干网络参数量为405万至6410万）。灰度图像被复制为RGB三通道，并使用模型内置的预处理与数据增强进行处理。训练流程包括冻结骨干网络的分类头训练，随后进行部分微调。评估指标涵盖分类性能、判别能力、效率以及可视化分析。结果：测试准确率呈非单调变化，从B0的95.93%到B1的96.95%；B7达到96.73%。B1取得了最高的准确率以及玻璃膜疣类别的最高F1分数（0.878……摘要至此被截断）。
tldr: 该研究发现固定分辨率迁移学习中EfficientNet家族内按规模缩放并不能单调提升SD-OCT视网膜疾病分类性能，最小的B1以96.95%的准确率超越更大的B7模型，表明在医学图像迁移学习中盲目增大模型并非最优选择。
en_tdlr: This study shows that within-family EfficientNet scaling under fixed-resolution transfer learning does not monotonically improve SD-OCT retinal disease classification, with the smallest B1 model (96.95% accuracy) outperforming the much larger B7, indicating that simply scaling up models is not optimal for medical image transfer learning.
